topics.topic: Contents and allowed cardinality of pending confirmations
questions: Does an OwnerSession hold one replaceable pending confirmation for the whole session, one per confirmable action kind, or several concurrent pending confirmations?
What facts constitute a pending confirmation, and does a session hold one pending confirmation in total, one per action, or several concurrently?
What facts constitute a pending confirmation, and can a session hold one pending confirmation in total, one per confirmable action, or several concurrent confirmations?

quotes:
An action that asks for confirmation (Identity formats) is submitted with a
   confirmation value Registry made when it showed the step: one-time, kept in
   the owner session, bound to the action, its target, the revision or access
   version the step showed, and its inputs — for the import, the file's digest
   and the picks. It is valid only in that session, for 10 minutes, and is
   used up by the first submission, whatever its answer; a refused submission
   needs the step shown again.
judgement.divergence: One implementation replaces the session's sole pending confirmation whenever another step is shown; another keeps several independently usable confirmation values, and the owner notices whether an earlier displayed confirmation still works.
judgement.why: A13 defines each confirmation value's contents and individual lifetime but neither text states how many may coexist or what showing another confirmation replaces.

topics.topic: Disclosure classification of uploaded files, containing sessions, and personal-data confirmation values
questions: Is the uploaded import file a `personal_data` OwnerSession fact because it contains imported customer and object values, or does the statement that every OwnerSession fact is `business_confidential` still apply to it?
What disclosure class applies to the uploaded import file and to pending confirmation values when they contain personal-data fields?
What disclosure class applies to the uploaded import file and to an OwnerSession containing it?

quotes: | `personal_data` | Project display name (R0-82); Object address, kind and characteristics (R0-38); Customer name, phone, e-mail, language, tax id, legal name (R0-80) |

| `business_confidential` | every other fact of every model: `project_id`, alias, status, revision, instants, the archived and anonymised marks; `customer_ref`, the Customer's kind, revision, instants and its erased, restricted and ended marks with their dates; `room_id`, room name and added instant; every artifact pointer fact; every agent session fact and the access request's text; every audit entry; the migration closure; the owner session |

Each fact has one class. An answer's class is the highest class of the facts
it carries (R0-26): the customer read, which carries the name beside the
marks, is `personal_data`; the customer list to the owner is too; the session's
access is `business_confidential`.

The owner uploads the export file (R0-72) in the owner interface. Registry
   reads it as data (A19) and answers the mapping without changing anything:
   each project the file holds, with its id, status, rooms and pointers; for
   each project the owner picks, the display name and alias it will arrive
   under (R0-85); each Customer the import will make, with the v1 value it
   comes from and the projects it will link (R0-80); every id that conflicts
   with one production holds.
judgement.why: The disclosure table classifies personal fields as `personal_data` but also classifies every OwnerSession fact as `business_confidential`, while M11 makes the uploaded file containing those fields an OwnerSession fact.
judgement.failure: a contradiction needs two quotes found verbatim in the texts

topics.topic: Requests and actions that update the last-request instant
questions: Which owner-interface actions or requests move the last-request instant?
Which requests move the last-request instant: every authenticated HTTP request, only reads and changes corresponding to product actions, or only state-changing owner actions?

Which requests move the last-request instant: every authenticated owner-interface request, only product actions, reads as well as changes, confirmation preparation and submission, import upload, and sign-out?

quotes:
The session ends at the first of: 8 hours after sign-in; 30 minutes without
   an owner request; the owner's sign-out; the instance's restart (M11 is never
   durable). An owner request is any request to the owner interface that
   carries the valid session, whatever its answer; it restarts the 30
   minutes.
judgement.why: State 2 defines an owner request as any owner-interface request carrying the valid session, regardless of its action or answer.

topics.topic: Uploaded import-file creation, replacement, consumption, and removal lifecycle
questions: Which product action creates or replaces this session fact, and which action reads and consumes it?
Which action creates or replaces the stored file, which action reads it, and what event counts as its use and removes it?
What product action uploads or replaces the file, which action reads it, and exactly when is it removed—on an import attempt, only after successful import, or also after a refused import?

quotes:
The owner uploads the export file (R0-72) in the owner interface. Registry
   reads it as data (A19) and answers the mapping without changing anything:
   each project the file holds, with its id, status, rooms and pointers; for
   each project the owner picks, the display name and alias it will arrive
   under (R0-85); each Customer the import will make, with the v1 value it
   comes from and the projects it will link (R0-80); every id that conflicts
   with one production holds.

The uploaded file is kept in the owner session that uploaded it, never in
   the store, until the import is confirmed, another file is uploaded in that
   session, or the session ends (M11); then it is dropped. The mapping names
   the file by its digest. The owner confirms that mapping in the confirmation
   step (A13 rule 6); the confirmation applies the file of that digest, the
   picks, names, aliases and Customer values the mapping showed, nothing
   else; a file no longer kept is refused and must be uploaded again.

An action that asks for confirmation (Identity formats) is submitted with a
   confirmation value Registry made when it showed the step: one-time, kept in
   the owner session, bound to the action, its target, the revision or access
   version the step showed, and its inputs — for the import, the file's digest
   and the picks. It is valid only in that session, for 10 minutes, and is
   used up by the first submission, whatever its answer; a refused submission
   needs the step shown again.
judgement.why: State 2 says upload creates or replaces the session file, mapping generation reads it, confirmation applies it, and confirmation, replacement, or session end drops it.

topics.topic: Pending-confirmation creation, access, replacement, and consumption lifecycle
questions: Which product actions create, read, replace and consume pending confirmation values, and does an attempted but refused confirmed action consume them?
Which product actions create, replace, read and clear pending confirmation values, and does a refused or failed confirmed action count as their being “used”?

quotes:
An action that asks for confirmation (Identity formats) is submitted with a
   confirmation value Registry made when it showed the step: one-time, kept in
   the owner session, bound to the action, its target, the revision or access
   version the step showed, and its inputs — for the import, the file's digest
   and the picks. It is valid only in that session, for 10 minutes, and is
   used up by the first submission, whatever its answer; a refused submission
   needs the step shown again. A submission becomes the first one when it
   passes the owner session and CSRF checks (A04 rule 6, stage 1): one refused
   before them leaves the value unused; from there on, whatever the answer —
   a value bound to another action included — the value is used up.
judgement.divergence: One implementation replaces an existing pending confirmation when any new confirmation step is shown; another retains both values until each is submitted, expires, or the session ends, and the owner notices whether the older confirmation remains usable.
judgement.why: A13 answers creation, binding, reading, expiry, and consumption—including consumption after a refused post-CSRF submission—but neither it nor M11 identifies what action replaces a still-pending value.

topics.topic: Creation and insertion of the OwnerSession CSRF value
questions: Who creates the CSRF value, and as part of which product action does it enter the OwnerSession?

topics.topic: Meaning and mutability of OwnerSession expiry
questions: Is this fact a fixed absolute latest-expiry instant, a current expiry instant that requests may move, or both as separate facts?

topics.topic: When the confirmation ID is created
questions: Is the confirmation id itself one of the pending values created before confirmation, or is it minted only when the pending confirmation is used successfully?

topics.topic: Whether OwnerSessions and mutable facts survive Registry restarts
questions: Does a Registry restart end every OwnerSession, or must the session and its newly added mutable facts survive restarts until normal session end?

topics.topic: Whether the mutable last-request instant is stored in OwnerSession
questions: Is OwnerSession an exception that carries a mutable instant, or is the last-request instant not a stored OwnerSession fact?

topics.topic: Whether the uploaded import file belongs to the OwnerSession model
questions: Is the uploaded import file a fact of the OwnerSession model, or transient input outside Registry's domain records?

topics.topic: Which transient OwnerSession facts are cleared when used
questions: Does “used” clear all three listed facts, or only pending confirmation values and the uploaded import file?
